title: Chapter 3253 Functional Fate
content:
Sunny remained silent for a short while, staring at Cassie intensely. Then, almost forcing himself, he slowly turned to Sable and sighed.

Who the hell were the Nine, indeed?

He was probably the best person to explain. After hesitating a little, Sunny spoke:

“They were nine people born in a peaceful realm... a realm called Thetis. Each of them was a confluence of myriad fates — ina sense, they were mortal avatars of fate, just like the Dragon is a mortal avatar of War God."

He pursed his lips.

“The Empire of War eventually conquered their kingdom and enslaved their people. However, just before that happened, the Nine had been sent to complete a sacred mission — they were meant to avenge their people, since they could not protect them. By destroying the Empire."

His expression darkened.

“The problem was that the Empire was protected by War God... so they needed to destroy War God first. And since they needed to destroy one of the gods, they deemed it necessary to destroy all the other gods as well — reasonably assuming that the rest of the pantheon would not just sit and watch as one of them gets obliterated."

Sable stared at him with a stunned expression.

After a long stretch of silence, she said in a subdued tone:

"Quite an... ambitious bunch, weren't they?"

Sunny spared Nephis a short glance, then nodded.

"Not only were they ambitious, but they were also incredibly tenacious. To the point that they actually succeeded, in the end. It is impossible to know whether an all-out war between the gods and the daemons would have happened without the Nine, but they definitely played a large role in bringing the world to its end. One could even say that they were the reason why it ended."

And now, the Nine were at the heart of this Nightmare.

‘But this is peculiar.'

The events of the Nightmare were usually connected to its Seed. But what connection was there between the Nine and Godgrave? Sunny contemplated it for a moment, then shook his head with a sigh.

“The Nine were not particularly powerful, though — most of them, at least. Rather, they were armed with the knowledge of fate and extremely skilled at manipulating the flow of history. They were impossibly driven, as well.”

Sable blinked a couple of times.

"Wait, wait. If these Nine were mortal men and women — and not particularly powerful, at that — then why would we declare a war on a literal god instead of simply killing them? It's a god! An actual god, people! What... am I missing something?"

Sunny smiled darkly.

"It's because the Nine are both mortal men and women and something far greater than that."

He sighed.

"They are fated. That alone does not really make them unique — I suspect there have been more than a few fated individuals etched into the pages of history. I myself have that Attribute, for example. However, nine Fated beings were born in the same place, at the same time... that cannot be a coincidence. Their existence points to something else."

He leaned back, considered his words for a few seconds, and then spoke in a concerned tone:

“It means that the Nine are not merely people, but rather a function of fate. And fate is all but impervious to change — it is like a vast river that only flows in one direction. You can throw a stone into the river and disturb its surface for a short while, but in the end, the current always wins."

Until, one day, it didn't.

Sunny and Cassie had destroyed fate once, but that was not something they could easily replicate. After all, that achievement was not theirs alone — a whole lot of events had to happen first to make their spectacular accomplishment possible.

And those events had not happened by accident, either. The nebulous figure of Weaver stood behind them, casting a deep shadow on everything it reached.

Fate had been undone... but that was only true for the real world. Here in the Nightmare, it still reigned supreme, which meant that its currents were tyrannical and stubborn.

Sunny glanced around the table with a dark expression.

“What I mean to say is that we can kill the members of the Nine once they are born... we can even destroy Thetis and slaughter everyone who lives there, preventing them from being born in the first place. But that will not destroy the Nine. Most likely, it will simply result in someone else becoming the Nine — someone else being chosen to personify that function of fate. The road to the end of the world will change, but the destination will remain the same."

He fell silent and frowned, thinking.

Cassie must have arrived at the same conclusion. Even then, it was not like she had been given all the time in the world — she seemed to have entered the Nightmare later than Nephis and Sunny, then spent a long while searching for Weaver's eye. It had taken her countless centuries to recover from the trauma of being exposed to the bare infinity of fate, and more time still to learn how to control her new power.

At the end of it all, she had to figure out a way to gather her scattered companions, restore their shattered spirits, and conquer the Nightmare.

Too numerous variables had to coincide in just the right way to make it possible. Sunny and Nephis — and Mordret, possibly — had to reach a state where they could be mended and would be willing to let her try. Most of all, Cassie had to determine the point in time after that moment arrived where a single action could result in the most seismic impact on the currents of fate, as well as the nature of that action.

And she seemed to have determined that the most impactful thing they could do was destroy the War Empire before it could devour Thetis — the moment they had to do it, meanwhile, was now.

Sunny sighed.

‘Damnation.'

That was all he had to say.

Sable, however, seemed to have a lot on her mind.

“Still! That's a god we are talking about, a god! A Divine being! No, not even a mere Divine being — one of the six great gods! War God, of all people... uh, gods!"

She covered her face with a palm and groaned.

“Couldn't you have at least chosen a less scary god? Like... Heart God! Heart God seems nice."

Remembering the Dreamspawn and the myths about the Heart Forest, Sunny shivered.

“What are you talking about? Heart God is probably the most harrowing of the six."

He paused for a few seconds, then scoffed.

"Believe it or not, killing a god is not entirely impossible. Eurys of the Nine did it once — and he was merely a Transcendent at the time. Another member of the Nine actually killed a Divine Titan twice."

Sable flinched.

“What? What kind of monster... who?"

Sunny smiled, then nodded at the dark figure leaning silently on the wall in a corner of the chamber.

"It was your good friend Orphne, if you really want to know."

Sable glanced at him with wide eyes, then turned to stare at Slayer.

Slayer showed no reaction at all, observing them with a cold indifference.

“S—sister Orphne?"

Sunny shrugged.

"I found her shadow in the Realm of Death. And killed it. Now she is one of the two Shadows that still follow me around."

He paused for a moment, then smiled.

"So, killing a god is not impossible. That is even if the Spell can truly manifest one of them — a real god in all their divine glory, not just a facsimile of a god. It couldn't in the lesser Nightmares."

Sunny knew that because, in a way, he had encountered the gods in his First Nightmare. It was the blessing of Shadow God he had received, not of the phantom of Shadow God. If the Spell could conjure gods as it wished, why would that happen?

Well, it made sense. People were accustomed to thinking about the Spell as some sort of omnipotent force, but in truth, even the Spell was bound by rules and restrictions. Even the Spell operated based on the resources in its possession. Manifesting each Nightmare drew on those resources, no doubt, just like using Aspect Abilities consumed soul essence... in fact, a particular Aspect Ability came to mind. That Ability belonged to none other than Cassie — it was her power to manifest memories into reality.

Cassie was limited in the number of memories she could manifest, and the strain on her essence grew heavier with the Rank of the being she tried to summon. She could not manifest creatures of a higher Rank than hers at all.

Who was to say that the Spell was any different?

Every year, myriad people faced their First Nightmare. But that was alright, because those Nightmares were modest in scope, populated by Dormant or Awakened beings. Second Nightmares were quite many, as well. Third Nightmares were rarer, and full of far more powerful creatures — scores of Corrupted abominations, and even a few Great ones. Sunny's own Third Nightmare had contained that damn Thieving Bird, as well. But, still, Third Nightmares were common by now.

The Fourth Nightmare, however... every Seed of that Category was a calamity, and only two had been conquered so far. Needless to say, the Fifth Nightmare was singular. More Category Five Gates could appear in the future, but for now, only one had ever been recorded.

The Spell was maintaining all of these Nightmares at the same time.

So, the question was... even if it could fully manifest a true god, would it sacrifice that immeasurable amount of resources for a Fifth Nightmare?

Sunny was not sure.

It was worth exploring, though.

In that moment, Nephis spoke, her voice even:

“Before we think about facing War God... shouldn't we consider something else first? The Empire is not just the Dragon, after all. It is also four Spirits, seven Supremes, and myriad seasoned legions."

Looking at Cassie, she paused for a moment, then asked:

“Are you sure that the five of us will be enough to defeat that?"

Cassie tilted her head a little.

"Five? No... but six of us? There's a chance."

She gestured to the door of the chamber.

"The Jade Queen. She's the sixth.”
